title: August Revolution (Vietnam, 1945)
summary: After Japan's surrender in August 1945, the Viet Minh seized power: in Hanoi on 19 August, in Hue by 23 August and in Saigon on 25 August. Sources date Emperor Bao Dai's abdication to 25 or 30 August. On 2 September Ho Chi Minh read the Declaration of Independence at Ba Dinh Square in Hanoi, founding the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.

uncertainty.note: The Library of Congress study dates the start of the uprising to 16-17 August. Bao Dai abdication: 25 August (LoC) or 30 August (Vietcetera).

as_recorded.value: On August 19, the Viet Minh and the people of Hanoi organized a massive demonstration.
Saigon fell on August 25 to the Viet Minh
On September 2, 1945, at Ba Dinh Square in Hanoi, President Ho Chi Minh reads the Declaration of Independence.

where.modern_name: Hanoi, Vietnam (also Hue and Saigon/Ho Chi Minh City)
where.historical_name: Hanoi, Tonkin, French Indochina under Japanese occupation

importance.justification: Founded the Democratic Republic of Vietnam; the sources place it at the start of the independence period.

related.because: Japan’s surrender left no ruling power in place in Vietnam, which the Viet Minh moved to fill.

sources.title: The General Uprising and Independence (Vietnam: A Country Study)
sources.publisher: Library of Congress Federal Research Division

sources.title: 1945 August Revolution: A triumph of patriotism and the aspiration for national independence

beats.caption: On 19 August 1945 crowds and self-defence forces in Hanoi seized the Northern Palace.
Hue had come under revolutionary control by 23 August, and Saigon followed on 25 August.
On 2 September at Ba Dinh Square, Ho Chi Minh read the Declaration of Independence, marking the founding of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.

reviewer_note: Two sources are Vietnamese outlets (state news agency and a media company); the Library of Congress study is the independent anchor. Dates conflict on Bao Dai abdication (25 vs 30 August) and on the start (16-19 August); the summary states both abdication dates.
